title: intmin
summary: Return the smallest value of an integer class.

gpu_support.notes: The like form creates a scalar on the prototype's exact GPU owner and preserves its integer class and complexity.

description: `intmin` returns the smallest value representable by an integer class. The default class is `int32`. Unsigned classes return zero. `intmin("like", prototype)` selects the class, complexity, and applicable placement from an integer prototype.
behaviors: Class-name forms support int8, int16, int32, int64, uint8, uint16, uint32, and uint64.
The result is a 1-by-1 scalar in the selected integer class. Signed minima remain exact and unsigned minima are zero.
A real or complex integer prototype selects the matching class and complexity. The imaginary component of a complex result is zero.
A gpuArray prototype produces a new scalar on the same registered provider and device without gathering the prototype.
A distributed prototype produces a distributed scalar with the same distribution scheme and does not materialize the full source value.

faqs.question: Does the like form copy the prototype shape?
faqs.answer: No. It always returns a 1-by-1 scalar; it copies the integer class, complexity, and applicable placement.

gpu_residency: The class-name forms return host scalars. The like form preserves an integer gpuArray prototype's exact provider, device, storage kind, and provenance.
gpu_behavior: The like form uploads only the scalar result. It does not download or otherwise materialize the prototype.
